title: The City That Paid People To Farm Rats
sources: Wikipedia, 'Great Hanoi Rat Massacre' (1902, French colonial Hanoi; bounty of 1 cent per rat tail; officials began noticing rats with no tails; bounty programme cancelled; historian Michael G. Vann)
Atlas Obscura, 'The Great Hanoi Rat Massacre of 1902' (rats spread through Hanoi's new sewer system; hired rat hunters went into the sewers; 7,985 rats killed in the last week of April 1902)
Saigoneer, 'The Great Hanoi Rat Massacre' (rats popping up in Hanoi's swankiest toilets; plague cases; over 20,000 rats killed in a single day in June 1902; tailless rats in the outskirts)

ScienceBlog summary of Vann's archive research (sewer crews killed 20,114 rats on 12 June 1902; public bounty of one cent per tail so offices didn't handle carcasses; an official found villagers breeding rats outside town)
Michael G. Vann, The Great Hanoi Rat Hunt (Oxford University Press, 2018)

lines.text: In 1902, the city of Hanoi paid people to get rid of rats,
lines.caps: In 1902, | the city | of Hanoi | paid | people | to get | rid of | rats,

lines.text: and somehow made the problem even worse.
See, the city had just built shiny new sewers,
and the rats loved them.
They popped out of fancy toilets,
and people feared the plague.
So the city hired rat catchers,
who caught over twenty thousand rats in one day.
lines.caps: who | caught | over | 20,000 | rats | in one | day.

lines.text: But the rats kept coming.
So the city made everyone a deal.
Bring us a rat's tail, and we'll pay you one cent.
lines.caps: Bring us | a rat's | tail, | and we'll | pay | you | 1 cent.

lines.text: Just the tail, so nobody had to carry dead rats.
And the tails came pouring in.
But then, officials noticed something weird.
Rats running around with no tails.
See, people caught a rat, snipped off the tail,
and let it go, to make more baby rats,
with brand new tails.
Some even started rat farms outside of town.
So the city canceled the deal,
because it wasn't getting rid of rats.
It was paying people to farm them.
